records.paraphrase: An unknown birth or conception time is proposed to be recovered through an astrology chart cast at the time of the question.
records.limitations: Distinct from natal forward prediction from independently recorded birth data.

records.paraphrase: Ten divisional chart positions are enlisted to infer missing ascendant/birth parameters.
records.limitations: No unique exact-time inversion shown by this sentence alone.

records.paraphrase: The chapter gives extensive physical, behavioral, familial and vocational descriptors for each of twelve possible rising signs.
records.limitations: Scoring must penalize broad multiple traits, contradictions, and self-reported observations already used to infer sign.

records.locator: Ch48 Aquarius rising passage, PDF131, around slokas42-45
records.paraphrase: The English rendition contrasts Satyacharya and Yavana negativity toward Aquarius or its Vargas with Chanakya's dissent.
records.limitations: Source preserves disagreement, not majority vote predictive validation.

records.paraphrase: Strong ascendant sign or strong ascendant lord is stated to make sign-level effects stronger.
records.limitations: Additional freedom unless strength computation and threshold fixed before human outcomes.

records.paraphrase: First and second Hora within each of twelve ascendants receive different body/behavior predictions, creating 24 finer categories.
records.limitations: A broad catalogue of traits is not an identification accuracy score.

records.paraphrase: First/second/third decanates of the twelve signs are separately described with physical, personal and wealth traits.
records.limitations: Many heterogeneous outcome adjectives; modern blinded scoring needs a frozen option-level mapping.

records.paraphrase: The work catalogs traits for nine Navamsas of each of twelve rising signs, including body measurements, personal disposition, roles and preferences.
records.limitations: 108 small classes and many adjectives increase overfitting opportunities; precise 3°20' boundaries and uncertainty critical.

records.paraphrase: The chapter says sign-level meanings also apply to D12 and Saptamsa-level interpretations can substitute for several other unlisted divisions.
records.limitations: This broadens post-hoc choices; cannot be implemented as universal substitution without defining rule scope and conflicts.

records.paraphrase: A horary ascendant within its first versus last 15° is used to assign the native's northern or southern solar course at birth.
records.limitations: Independent source text check needed for boundary equality at exactly 15°.

records.paraphrase: Season at birth is assigned from strongest horary ascendant occupant or its decanate ruler; if solar-course/season disagree, some planet assignments are exchanged.
records.limitations: The text offers an explicit override; must freeze the exact conflict test and priority.

records.paraphrase: The section proposes natal Moon/Ascendant via horary 1st/5th/9th strength, natal Moon's sign, a person's touched body part, or geometrical reflected distance.
records.limitations: Alternative paths must be evaluated separately, not cherry-picked based on the known birth chart.

records.paraphrase: Person standing, lying down, seated or rising is used to choose 1st/4th/7th/10th sign from horary ascendant as natal ascendant.
records.limitations: Requires prospective video/observation of posture at independently timestamped query; not birth-derived forward prediction.

records.paraphrase: Name given by parents, phonetic matras and measured shadow length are transformed into a proposed birth nakshatra.
records.limitations: Name standardization, language, pronunciation and shadow measurement introduce unrecorded inputs; formula must be deterministic.

records.paraphrase: An alternative recovery method multiplies horary ascendant longitude by sign- and occupant-dependent factors, then uses different divisors for birth year/season/tithi/navamsa/time; permits adding or subtracting nine for anomalous output.
records.limitations: The 'anomalistic answers' correction creates ex-post flexibility unless exact admission and sign of correction are predeclared.

records.paraphrase: The author reports that the lost-horoscope rules attributed to Yavana and Bhadasana contain ambiguities and asks the student to exercise judgment.
records.limitations: Keep an explicit source-level unresolved state: do not fill the gaps through personality fit.

records.paraphrase: Second rectification path uses horary Moon's sign, daylight category, degrees and sign multiplication to infer natal Moon/nakshatra, including plus/minus-nine name/count adjustment.
records.limitations: Variant choice, special Pisces condition and sequence must be fixed before tests.

records.paraphrase: The Portuguese-translated Parashara dialogue proposes to reconstruct unknown year/season/month/tithi/star/ascendant and divisional details from a Prashna ascendant.
records.limitations: Second-hand Portuguese translation: a parallel tradition, not independent observed success.

records.paraphrase: Rasi D12 of horary ascendant is linked with birth-year Jupiter; first/second Hora to solar course, decanate ruler to birth season, with swaps if contradictory.
records.limitations: Compare with Saravali Ch52.1-3; similar formulations may share textual source; do not multiply witnesses.

records.paraphrase: The subject's approximate age and multiples of Jupiter's 12-year cycle are used to select a candidate birth year.
records.limitations: The method is not a blind recovery from a natal chart; it explicitly consumes outside age information.

records.paraphrase: After estimating natal season/day, the solar longitude difference and solar motion in kalas are used to reconstruct elapsed local time relative to sunrise.
records.limitations: Exact original Sanskrit astronomical definitions, unit conversion and boundary assumptions unresolved.

records.locator: Adhyaya II sloka23, printed p36-37 / PDF454-455
records.paraphrase: The ancient translated sloka gives planet rulers of the six Indian seasons associated with decanate assignment.
records.limitations: Jataka printed verse and translator's lost-horoscope note must remain distinct.
records.source_layer: Sastri edition: original verse versus editor comments flagged explicitly

records.locator: Adhyaya II commentary to sloka23, printed p37 / PDF455
records.paraphrase: Sastri's notes explain guessing birth season from the strongest planet in a query ascendant or decanate ruler if empty.
records.limitations: Commentary-layer formula parallels Saravali Ch52 and BPHS 5496–5500; not independent ancient verse or empirical confirmation.
records.source_layer: Sastri edition: original verse versus editor comments flagged explicitly

records.locator: Adhyaya II commentary to sloka23, printed p37-38 / PDF455-456
records.paraphrase: Sastri adds his own example of progression/aspects and seasons when explaining the original Indian season rulers.
records.limitations: An editor's progressions are not automatically part of Vaidyanatha's classical computational specification.
records.source_layer: Sastri edition: original verse versus editor comments flagged explicitly

model_boundary.natal_forward: Requires independent known DOB/time/place -> predicted answers
model_boundary.traditionally_rectified_horary: Uses query-time sky plus age, name, posture, body part touched or shadow; reverse-estimation family
model_boundary.admission: Must freeze distinct algorithms and all external observation inputs; do not use born-time truth to select alternatives.
